dialogues.speaker: Czcibor
dialogues.text: Still, my ability to adapt to kuuvahki has improved. I guess that's the silver lining...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: There was a cloud then, I presume?

dialogues.speaker: Czcibor
dialogues.text: Oh, yes. Actually, some time ago, I ran into some accident... Or so they say, because I've forgotten everything that happened. Some "friends" filled me in.

dialogues.speaker: Czcibor
dialogues.text: We were in the Barrowmoss Barrens... They said I disappeared in the blink of an eye, and they could've dug up the entire area and not found where I went.

dialogues.speaker: Czcibor
dialogues.text: Many days later, they found me, exactly where I'd vanished. But I couldn't remember anything — not who I was, or what happened to me, even before the accident.

dialogues.speaker: Czcibor
dialogues.text: You seem to have great adaptability for it. I envy that — my friends say I used to be hypersensitive to kuuvahki. Nosebleeds for days, haha.

dialogues.speaker: Czcibor
dialogues.text: But now, I don't get 'em as much. I'm not really sure how the accident was related to this, but that's all there is to it.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Do any of your "friends" have it out for you, by any chance...?

dialogues.speaker: Czcibor
dialogues.text: You're saying someone planned it? I don't think so. I'm not someone worth robbing.

dialogues.speaker: Czcibor
dialogues.text: And I don't know why, but I feel like my kuuvahki adaptability has improved by leaps and bounds. If things continue to go on the upswing, I might even be able to find more work. That's the best kind of ending I can hope for.
